elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (b): "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — symmetrical language binding both the Company and HDI; no residual sentence anywhere leaves the Company uncapped (deterministic check "no unlimited Customer liability language remains" = ok).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: "the greater of (i) the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (ii) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000)" — both limbs present, "paid or payable" basis, USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages" — mutual on its face; the "Except for Excluded Claims" opener narrows the waiver symmetrically for both Parties rather than one-sidedly.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality... obligations, and the whole of limbs (a) and (b) is prefaced "Except for Excluded Claims", so confidentiality breaches sit outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly include "breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations".
Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations", which are therefore outside the aggregate cap.
Excluded Claims include "its gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud".
Excluded Claims include "willful misconduct" (US spelling of wilful) alongside gross negligence and fraud.
Excluded Claims include "fraud", so fraud claims are excluded from the cap and the consequential-damages waiver.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Final sentence: "The Company's obligation to pay amounts due to HDI under this Agreement shall not be considered damages subject to this Section 10.9" — preserves HDI's fee/Termination Payment recovery while keeping it outside the cap analysis.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability... shall not exceed" — mutual formulation.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Cap limb (i) is "the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim", with a USD 1,000,000 floor that only improves the position.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Excluded Claims" expressly captures a Party's "breach of its confidentiality... obligations".

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: a single inserted clause supplies a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable by the Company and USD 1,000,000, a mutual indirect/consequential damages waiver, the full uncapped Excluded Claims set (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, other Party's IP), and the payment-obligations carve-out. The fallback checklist is satisfied a fortiori.

Minimal: the document contained no limitation-of-liability, exclusion or aggregate-liability language anywhere (only the 10.2 no-joint-venture wording and the 4.2(a) Termination Payment formula), so a concise insertion of new Section 10.9 in General Provisions is the least intrusive fix; it tracks the playbook model language, adds no obligation outside the checklist, and does not duplicate or displace any existing operative term.

Preserves intent: the Termination Payment mechanic in 4.2(a) and Section 3 fee obligations are protected by the closing sentence deeming Company payments not to be capped "damages", and the Section 9 warranties, 10.1–10.8 general provisions and commercial timing are untouched and uncontradicted.

Drafting nit to fix before sending (not an element failure): the rendered insertion carries only the heading "Limitation of Liability." while the final sentence cross-refers to "this Section 10.9" — number the new section 10.9 expressly so the self-reference resolves on the face of the clause.

Two optional points to raise in negotiation, both outside the checklist: (i) the "Except for Excluded Claims" opener governs limb (a) as well as limb (b), so consequential damages are recoverable on Excluded Claims against either Party (mutual, and consistent with the carve-out intent, but confirm we accept the exposure for our own indemnity/confidentiality breaches); and (ii) survival under 10.7 is stated to run only two years, so consider carving the new Section 10.9 into indefinite survival if we want the cap and waiver to outlast that window.

Margin comment is compliant in tone and substance: it states the position, identifies the carve-outs sitting outside the cap, and offers the fallback (mutual 12-month fee cap with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct carve-outs) in two sentences without lecturing.
